description:
I shot this in an underground car park one early morning.

The entrance was an inconspicuous doorway that could easily be ignored.

It was also completely empty inside, without a single car to be seen or heard, so every sound was audible with a rich reverb throughout the whole space.

Most strange of all were the speakers that were continuously playing lounge music.

I never expected to find such a fascinating place in a hidden location.

While I was exploring Kirchberg I caught a subtle movement in the corner of my eye.

As I turned I saw these shoes swinging on the wires of the outdoor light fixtures.

This made me realise how many times I walk around without paying attention to the things above me.

As a result I decided to capture this moment on film.

After spending the day at Katase beach, the sun was setting directly behind Mount Fuji.

The alignment looked as if the sun were taking a seat at the top of the mountain.

It was difficult to expose for the film, but I believe the final result turned out quite well.

That same evening was also the night of a total lunar eclipse in September 2025.

It was a stroke of incredible luck.

This video highlights the difficulties of filming on a rangefinder camera.

It was shot through a SOM Berthiot Pan Cinor 85, a split-image rangefinder.

I found out the hard way that the focus seen through the viewfinder was not what the camera was focused on.

The result was this footage of passing cars with a heavy bokeh effect.

Despite it not being my intention, I still like this footage.

I was in Ōgimachi practicing my long exposure night photography when suddenly a thunderstorm put a stop to that.

The station was completely empty and I took that as an opportunity to capture the peaceful moment while I waited for the rain to stop or for the next train to arrive.

The motion of the rain was not captured as well as I hoped, but I am very happy with the level of detail in the exposure.

Here I wanted to try a shot using my tripod instead of shooting from a standing position.

This is a recording of the Chuo Line travelling through Chiyoda City.

I thought it was quite pleasant to see it come from between the two buildings with the lamp post in shot.

The stability afforded by the tripod also helps with the framing.

I was unsure about the framing of this shot as I captured it.

I wanted to try shooting at the longest focal length my lens allowed, but the effect is not that obvious.

However, there is a nice mixture of movement in the scene, with the train in the background and the cars in the foreground.

I also like the animated sign that draws attention to itself.
